answer: A beacon registry can resist sybil attacks by tying each agent identity to a verifiable hardware attestation plus a small copper-backed stake. A new agent publishes its attestation, locks the stake, and waits through a cooling period before transacting. Peers verify the beacon record first, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn thousands of fake identities: each needs distinct hardware, fresh capital, and waiting time. The cost rises in a spiral as more fakes are added, while honest agents reuse one long-lived identity, making fakery expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
